issues.description: default_raise sentinel pattern persists despite removing its stated reason for existing.
issues.detail: Comments still say default_factory=default_raise is for <3.10 compatibility, but 3.9 is gone. The kw_only dataclass now actually enforces required kwargs natively. The factory-that-raises is incidental complexity left over from the workaround era; it complects required-field semantics with a runtime error masquerading as a default. Remove the indirection and just declare the field required.
issues.lines: around default_raise and field(default_factory=default_raise) call sites

issues.description: Repeated @dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True) inlined where one named decorator would say it once.
issues.detail: The PR removed kw_only_dataclass and replaced ~15 call sites with the literal @dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True). That is easy (mechanical) but not simple: the intent has a name, and the name was useful. Reintroducing a one-line alias (now unconditional) keeps the value of "this class is a kw-only frozen record" expressed once.

issues.description: install.sh version gate still references Python 3.7 as the lower bound.
issues.detail: The error string was updated to say >=3.10, but the actual numeric check is PYTHON_MINOR_VER -lt 7. The message and the predicate now disagree about what the code is actually about. Two facts (the displayed minimum and the enforced minimum) are complected in two places and have drifted. Make the bound a single value and derive both.

issues.description: Amazon/Rocky install steps run dnf search inside CI provisioning with no consumer of the output.
issues.detail: dnf search python3.12 is a debugging artifact, not a step. It is incidental noise that will silently slow CI and confuse future readers about whether the search result gates anything (it does not). Drop it; the dnf install line is the actual fact being asserted.
issues.lines: Prepare Amazon Linux / Prepare Rocky steps

issues.description: option() in cmd_classes.py now uses MISSING as default, but callers relying on the old None fallback are not audited in the diff.
issues.detail: Before, on <3.10, default_default was None; on >=3.10 it was MISSING. The new code unconditionally uses MISSING. That is correct for kw_only frozen dataclasses, but any caller that depended on "no default supplied means None" silently changes semantics. The value/identity question (what does "no default" mean here?) deserves an explicit answer in a comment or a check.

review.summary: This is a straightforward removal of 3.9 compatibility scaffolding and is mostly SIMPLE — incidental complexity from version-gating is being correctly deleted. The remaining smells are leftover workarounds whose justification just evaporated: default_raise sentinels, the named kw_only_dataclass helper inlined everywhere, and stale version numbers in shell scripts and comments. None are blockers; all are opportunities to finish the decomposition this PR started. The hammock question that should have been asked: now that kw_only is native, what other workarounds in this file are no longer earning their keep?
